title: How to Find Subscriptions You Forgot About (India)
html:
In India, forgotten subscriptions hide in four places: UPI AutoPay mandates, card e-mandates, Google Play, and your email. Check each one. Cancel in the place that bills you, not in the app: deleting an app cancels nothing.

Last updated: 10 Oct 2026.

I ran this check on my own phone, a vivo V23 Pro on Android 14 (Funtouch OS 14), on 11 Oct 2026.

1. UPI AutoPay mandates

A UPI AutoPay mandate lets a company collect repeat payments from your bank account. NPCI says you can pause or revoke a mandate at any time. Open your UPI app and find the section that lists your AutoPay or mandates. Check the merchant, amount and how often it is charged. Cancel the ones you do not use.

In Google Pay on my vivo V23 Pro, tap the You tab at the bottom right. The list on that screen has an Autopay row (mine said "No pending requests"), and that is where recurring UPI payments are managed. I checked this on 11 Oct 2026.

2. Card e-mandates

Subscriptions charged to a card are e-mandates. The RBI's Digital Payments - E-mandate Framework, 2026 (issued 21 April 2026) sets rules that help you here:

  • A mandate can be registered only after an additional factor of authentication (AFA), such as an OTP or app approval.
  • Your bank or card issuer must send you a notification at least 24 hours before each charge. It must show the merchant's name, the amount, the date and time of the debit, the e-mandate reference and the reason.
  • Recurring transactions up to Rs 15,000 can go through without AFA. For insurance premiums, mutual fund subscriptions and credit card bill payments, the limit is Rs 1,00,000. Above these, AFA is required.
  • You have a right to opt out of a particular transaction or of the whole e-mandate, and the opt-out is confirmed to you.

So read those pre-debit messages instead of deleting them. A charge you do not recognise is a reason to open your bank or card app and look for the mandate.

3. Google Play

On Android, open the Play Store, tap your profile picture, go to Payments and subscriptions, then Subscriptions. Select the subscription and tap Cancel subscription. Google says that when you cancel you can still use the subscription for the time you have already paid for, and that uninstalling the app does not cancel it. Google Pay's help adds that payments already made are not refunded. On my phone, the Payments and subscriptions screen lists Payment methods, Purchase verification, Subscriptions, Budget and history and Redeem code, and Subscriptions is the one to open.

4. Your email

Search your inbox for words such as "receipt", "subscription", "renews", "trial" and "invoice". This finds anything billed directly by the company, including services that do not show up in the places above. Look at the last 12 months, because yearly renewals do not appear in a single month.

Trial and bundle traps

A free trial is a subscription that has not started charging yet. When you start one, set a reminder before the first charge, or cancel straight away. Many services let you keep access until the trial ends. Check any phone plan or card offer that includes a free subscription too: it can turn into a paid one when the offer ends.

What to do next

  1. Open your UPI apps and list AutoPay mandates. Cancel what you do not use.
  2. Look at card mandates and the pre-debit messages from your bank.
  3. Open Play Store, Payments and subscriptions, Subscriptions.
  4. Search your email for receipts, and total what you find by the year.
  5. Add a calendar reminder every six months. Also make sure a leaked email or password is not behind a charge: see how to check for a data breach.
